headline_tag: uptrend holds, but price stays soft as US rate-rise odds climb

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. Apply it carefully for now: Bitcoin has been under its 50-day average for 17 days (about 7% below it), the mood reads extreme fear at 25 out of 100, price is only about 4% above its 200-day average of $73,195, and a strong US jobs report has raised the odds of a Fed rate rise on 8 December. So keep any increase small and easy to pause, lead with trust, safety and explainer messages, speed up only once price closes back above about $81,901, and pause the increase if price closes below $73,195. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

A close below $73,195 would put the long-run uptrend in question, while a close back above $78,000 would ease the pressure.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the next week looks soft to neutral. At about $75,901, Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 17 days, sits about 7% below it and about 10% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed is at 25, which is extreme fear; news is taking a little more off the week, because a much stronger US jobs report (165,000 new jobs against about 65,000 expected) raised the odds of a December Fed rate rise (PANews). A normal week swings about $3,971, so a close above $78,000 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $73,195 (the 200-day average) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. Calmer rate news would steady the week, while a close under $73,195 is the cue for safety-first messaging.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 17% higher and about 90% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 7% and a lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which can make any further dip sharper. Price must win back $81,901 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. US news cuts both ways: the rule allowing crypto in 401(k) retirement plans has gone to the White House for final review (Bloomberg via PANews), while the US Treasury is cutting exchange MEXC off from US banks, and the next Fed meeting is on 8 December, so keep bigger campaign pushes for a reclaim of the 50-day average.

The 3-6 month picture leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 4% above its 200-day average, which is still rising about 4% over 90 days, while Bitcoin remains about 39% below its all-time high; news is adding a little here, as Russia's central bank approved Bitcoin, Ether and USDT for retail trading (PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,195 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,769 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.

items.theme: Regulators tighten on exchanges, and some apps pause
items.why: The US Treasury ordered US banks to stop handling money for exchange MEXC, alleging at least $16 billion in sanctions-evasion transactions, and Thailand's regulator filed a criminal complaint against Bitget's operator and will block it from 5 December. In Brazil, Nubank and Mercado Pago both paused crypto transfers citing provider or system problems, and Binance says it will reopen withdrawals for HYPE, INJ, APT, NEAR and LTC before next weekend after its theft.
items.marketing_angle: A good week for content on licensed, locally supervised platforms and how to keep assets safe, without naming or attacking other exchanges.

items.why: Hyperliquid Strategies, a Nasdaq-listed company that holds HYPE, says a subsidiary has applied to register as a US futures broker so it can carry US client accounts on Hyperliquid's approved markets. A separate filing shows the company holds about 16% of HYPE's circulating supply after buying about 9.1 million tokens in the third quarter. HYPE is up about 2% on the day but down about 12% over the week; the reports give no single reason for the weekly fall.
items.marketing_angle: An explainer topic on what on-chain trading apps are and why US approval matters, for users already curious about HYPE.

items.theme: Tokenized stocks keep spreading, with pushback
items.why: HTX says it will list US stock tokens on 9 November, Robinhood's CEO says tokenized stocks are already live on Robinhood Chain, and SBI's Japanese share token went live on HashKey. At the same time, 67 companies including Meta and Palantir have objected to their shares being traded as tokens on the OKX and ICE platform, according to its public notice.
items.marketing_angle: Useful education content on what a tokenized stock is and what the holder actually owns, a topic competitors are also covering.

items.why: A much stronger jobs report pushed traders toward a December Fed rate rise (CME FedWatch had 72.8% before the release) and the Fed's Daly said policy may need to tighten further, which usually weighs on crypto.

items.why: If finalised, US retirement savings plans could offer crypto, opening a large new channel of long-term money (Bloomberg via PANews).

items.headline: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Operator, to Block Platform From Dec 5
items.why: Another Asian regulator is moving against unlicensed exchanges, which tightens the field but mostly affects one platform.

items.headline: Bank of Russia Approves Bitcoin, Ether, USDT and Other Cryptocurrencies for Retail Trading
items.why: A major central bank opening retail access to Bitcoin and other coins widens the legal base of buyers over time.

items.headline: US Treasury and Federal Reserve Withdraw Proposal to Lower Threshold for Cross-Border Transfer "Travel Rule"
items.why: Dropping a 2020 plan to cut the reporting threshold from $3,000 to $250 removes a possible extra paperwork burden on crypto transfers.

summary.short: A much stronger US jobs report raised the odds of a December Fed rate rise, and two Brazilian apps paused crypto transfers, so news leans negative for the week.
summary.medium: US enforcement against MEXC and Thailand's action against Bitget weigh a little, partly offset by the 401(k) crypto rule reaching final White House review.
summary.long: Russia's central bank approving retail crypto trading and the withdrawn US travel-rule tightening are small structural positives.
